items.text: Miranda E. Hernandez works in the Criminal Appeals Division of the Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office. She previously served as deputy director of legislative affairs there, counsel to the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee, and a political appointee at the U.S. Department of Justice. She holds a J.D. and M.B.A. from Northern Illinois University. Her campaign’s top priorities are improving quality of life and maternal health outcomes, funding law enforcement and public safety, and ensuring fairness in property tax appeals. Her campaign says she advanced state legislation to strengthen protections for sexual assault and domestic violence survivors, and a bill allowing first-time, non-violent gun offenders to apply for a FOID card after completing a court-approved diversion program.
